T-001.Title: Wire the existing postProcessPeleSvg into ExportHtml.renderPele before SVG insertion and appearance application

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add exactly one import to src/muya/lib/utils/exportHtml.js — `import { postProcessPeleSvg } from '../parser/render/pelePipeline'` (placed with the other parser/render imports) — reusing the actual existing named export, not a duplicate body, a parallel policy, a helper extraction/move or a type-detection redesign. pelePipeline.js, peleOptions.js, diagramAppearance.js, the Muya public export methods and all other sources stay byte-identical; the import adds no initialization cycle, no top-level effects and no editor mutations or observers to export execution.

In renderPele (START_BLOCK_EXPORT_PELE_RENDER), replace `peleContainer.innerHTML = rendered.svg` with `peleContainer.innerHTML = postProcessPeleSvg(rendered.svg, rendered.type)` placed immediately before the unchanged `applyDiagramAppearance(peleContainer, rawCode, this.muya?.diagramAppearance?.getExportOverride(index - 1, rawCode))` call, so appearance application remains the last step per diagram. Post-processing consumes the actual pele render result's `rendered.type` — never a separately guessed or re-detected type — and preserves render options, measurement font, idPrefix/index allocation (`pele-export-${index++}` with `index - 1` for the override), the `mermaid` wrapper class, the invalid-code placeholder and the catch boundary; a post-processing failure follows the existing export error path without an unhandled rejection.

Coverage is structural, not per-branch: both Muya public export APIs (Muya#exportHtml → renderHtml, Muya#exportStyledHTML → generate) and the editor.vue styledHtml/docx/pdf/print consumers all reach renderPele through renderHtml, so the single insertion covers them with no editor.vue or Muya API change.
